findings.claim: numericID no longer wraps the strconv error. The cause is lost: errors.Is(err, strconv.ErrSyntax/ErrRange) and errors.As(*strconv.NumError) stop matching. An all-digit id that overflows int64 used to carry 'value out of range' in the message. It now reports only 'not a number', which is wrong for a numeric id and gives no hint of the real cause. Dropping %w for a purely cosmetic duplication of the id trades away diagnostic information and the error chain. Keeping %w and reporting only the NumError's Err, or stating the range case separately, would have kept the cause without repeating the id.

evidence: The diff replaces fmt.Errorf(..., %w, err) with a format that has no %w, so the parse error is discarded.
The new test only checks that the id string appears once. It does not cover the out-of-range case or error unwrapping.
